passage: Daniel had a lab shift until seven in Glasgow on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and Kwame worked evenings at a hotel in Accra on other days. For a month their calls had been random, one of them always tired or busy. On a Sunday morning they sat down, each with a paper calendar, and did it properly. "Tuesday at eight my time, after the lab. Friday at ten, before your shift." "And Sunday?" "Sunday is the long one. Two hours, no phones, no other tabs." They wrote it in permanent pen. That week Kwame's Tuesday call started at five past eight because a bus was late, and neither minded. On Sunday they talked for two hours and did not notice the light change.

qa.q: At what time on Tuesdays did Daniel and Kwame agree to call?
qa.a: They agreed to call at eight, Daniel's time, after the lab.

qa.q: What is Kwame feeling about the new arrangement?
qa.a: Kwame seems relieved and settled, since the calls no longer depend on who is tired, and the late bus does not bother anyone.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the couple add for a week when a call must be missed, and why?
qa.a: They could exchange a short voice message that day, because a small contact keeps the link alive when the live call cannot happen.

qa.q: How might Daniel see the long Sunday slot?
qa.a: Daniel gets two uninterrupted hours with no other tabs, which makes it feel like time set aside for the relationship and not squeezed between lab work.

grounding: Shows a couple fixing regular call times around lab hours and shifts, with one weekend slot kept for a long conversation.

passage:
The chemistry lab emptied at six, and Ramesh stayed behind at the long bench with his lab timetable, his phone propped against a beaker rack. On the screen, Pema sat in the hospital staff room in Gangtok, still in her nurse's uniform, a shift roster in her hand.
'Okay,' Ramesh said, 'my labs run till six on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. Wednesday nights I also have group study at nine.'
'And I'm on nights Thursday to Saturday.' She ran a finger down the roster. 'So Monday at nine, Tuesday at nine, and Wednesday at seven-thirty, before your group?'
'Seven-thirty works.'
'Done.' She wrote it on the back of the roster. 'And Sunday morning? The long one. No rushing.'
'Sunday, ten o'clock, as long as we want.'
They both took a photo of their notes. Two weeks later, the lab assistant teased Ramesh for leaving at exactly 8:55 every Monday.

qa.q: When is the long weekend call?
qa.a: Sunday, ten o'clock, as long as they want.

qa.q: How does Pema seem to feel about the Sunday slot?
qa.a: She seems eager and relieved to have one unhurried call, asking for 'the long one' with no rushing.

qa.q: What could the couple do if a hospital shift suddenly changes?
qa.a: Agree now on a quick message to move that call to the next free evening, so one change does not throw off the whole week.

qa.q: How does the new routine look to the lab assistant?
qa.a: The lab assistant notices Ramesh leaving at exactly 8:55 every Monday and teases him, seeing the plan has become a steady habit.

grounding: Shows a couple fitting three weekly calls around lab hours and a nursing roster, with one long Sunday call kept free.

passage:
Dear Yamini,
You asked how Kartik and I are managing now that he's working in Dubai and I'm stuck in labs till seven. Honestly, the first month was a mess: missed calls, him calling while I had gloves on, me calling when he was asleep.
So last Sunday we sat down on a video call with both our timetables. My lab days are Monday, Tuesday and Thursday. His airport shift runs 2 p.m. to 11 p.m. his time. We picked three short calls: Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 p.m. my time, which falls in his break. And Saturday morning is the long one: no cooking, no laundry, just us.
One week in, no missed calls. I actually look forward to Wednesdays now.
Come visit soon and I'll tell you the rest.
Bhavna

qa.q: How did Bhavna feel during the first month, and how now?
qa.a: Bhavna felt frustrated by the missed calls and bad timing, and now feels relieved and even looks forward to Wednesdays.

qa.q: What else could Bhavna and Kartik add to the plan?
qa.a: A quick text rule for days when a call has to move, so a long lab or shift does not turn into a missed call and hurt feelings.

qa.q: How might Kartik experience the 10:30 p.m. calls?
qa.a: For Kartik they fall in his break, so he can talk without rushing or being woken up, which makes the calls easier.

grounding: Shows a couple matching lab days and work shifts to set three short weekly calls plus one long weekend call.
